q: The Minimum Description Length (MDL) principle for model selection chooses the model M that minimises the two-part code length L(M) + L(data|M). Its connection to Bayesian model selection is:
opts: MDL always equals MAP (maximum a posteriori)
MDL corresponds to Bayesian model selection with a non-informative (Jeffreys) prior in the limit
MDL minimises the AIC (Akaike Information Criterion)
MDL requires knowing the true model class
exp: MDL with the normalized maximum likelihood (NML) code corresponds to Bayesian model selection with the Jeffreys prior (invariant prior in information geometry). Both penalise model complexity by the number of parameters times (log n)/2.
